query: The Outside Ledge {From the window at the top, a ledge a foot wide runs round the outside of the tower. From the far side, they say, you can see all seven towers and every bridge at once.|The ledge. Someone has chalked a tiny arrow on the sill: THIS WAY, BRAVE ONE.|You know the ledge's handholds now: the gargoyle's ear, the iron ring, the crack shaped like a smile.} {The wind is mild.|{season == "winter": There's ice on the stone.|A crow is sitting exactly where you'd put your foot.}|The bridges below are just lighting up for evening.} Edge round the ledge {You reach the far side and there they are, seven towers, every bridge of light, the lake holding the whole castle upside down. You forget to be afraid until the way back.|You inch round past the arrow and stand, breathing, over the whole academy. Somebody far below waves. You wave back like a fool.|Ear, ring, smile. You're round in a minute and sit with your feet over the drop, the castle lit up below like a map of itself.} {Your foot slips on the first step and you spend a long moment hugging the wall. You climb back in through the window shaking and scraped.|The wind takes your scarf and very nearly you. You crawl back inside on grazed hands and sit on the floor a while.|You misjudge the crack shaped like a smile. Your knee meets the stone hard, and you retreat, limping.} Look out from the window {You lean on the sill and look out at the three towers you can see. It's enough. It's more than enough.|You stay inside and read the chalk arrow until it stops sounding like a dare.|You stay at the window and watch the bridges light, one by one, without needing to see them all.}
